options.B: An efficient and effective means of diagnosing illness
options.C: Provision of a physical connection between physician and client leading to establishment of trust
options.D: Billing requirements of Medicaid and Medicare that mandate a physical examination

correctAnswerSourceText: B & C. The physician–client relation-
explanation: ship is extremely valuable. The history, observation, and physical examination of the client have essentially led to medicine being viewed as an art. In addition to diagnosing a problem and promoting health, strong connections form between physician and client. The client permits the physician to touch his body, and the physician demonstrates fidelity to the relationship by taking time to see, hear, and feel what the client’s body reveals. Trust is fostered and is beneficial to both parties. A routine assessment is the definition of a physical examination. Medicaid and Medicare do require a certain portion of a physical examination for physician reimbursement for services.

question: Female clients are encouraged to receive regularly scheduled health care screenings and examinations throughout each pregnancy. The primary value of prenatal care is to:

options.A: Detect clients who are at risk for preterm delivery
options.B: Assess the client and baby for genetic defects. 395
options.C: Monitor the health of the mother and baby
options.D: Determine if a vaginal birth is expected

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Monitoring the health status of both
explanation: client and baby provides support and education, detects problems, and allows timely intervention and planning. Prenatal care includes a comprehensive assessment to detect high-risk issues for both client and baby.

question: A client asks the nurse, “Will my immune system be weaker by relying on a vaccine for protection?” The nurse informs the client that:

options.A: The immune system works in healthy people but not in those with illness
options.B: A vaccine offers some degree of immunity for a limited time
options.C: Exposure to the natural disease strengthens the immune system better than a vaccine
options.D: The immune system makes antibodies against a germ whether the germ is encountered naturally or by receiving a vaccine

correctAnswerSourceText: D. The immune system mounts a
explanation: response to an antigen. The immune system does not differentiate between antigens occurring in the environment and those administered in a vaccine. People with an illness will have varying degrees of immune system activity depending on what type of illness they have. Some vaccines require booster doses while others impart lifetime immunity.

question: A client who will be flying nonstop from New York to Tokyo is seen in the travel clinic today. The nurse knows the client understands the teaching regarding deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prevention when he replies:

options.A: I will take an aspirin prior to departure
options.B: I need to stretch and move about the plane every 1 to 2 hours
options.C: I should drink 8 ounces of water midway through the flight
options.D: I should drink an alcoholic beverage to relax

correctAnswerSourceText: B. To prevent venous stasis and DVT
explanation: formation, the client should flex and extend the foot, move each foot in a circular pattern, and contract the lower extremity muscles frequently throughout the flight. In addition, walking the aisle enhances venous and lymphatic return. Aspirin prevents platelet aggregation but is not recommended therapy to prevent DVT. Maintaining adequate hydration is healthy. Eight ounces of water is not an adequate intake for such a flight. Alcoholic beverages do not precipitate DVT but may make the client sleepy, resulting in failure to exercise the lower extremities.

question: The nurse understands that the best predictor of health behavior and long-lasting successful behavior change is the:

options.A: Culture in which a client lives
options.C: Reading level and education of the client

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Most health promotion strategies
explanation: assist the individual to change risky behaviors but the long-term failure rate is high. The most successful strategies change the community culture to one of health promotion by involving the client, family, media, employers, educators, faith communities, organizations, health care, and government. Factors in the community culture that continue to place individuals at risk are changed. Age is not a deterrent to positive change. Literacy is important but illiterate individuals can adapt to positive change by learning methods other than reading. Chronic illness may motivate a client initially but the reversion rate to old habits is high. Health promotion is focused basically on healthy people to prevent illness, disability, and death.

question: As the nurse in a primary care clinic, you teach selfbreast exams to all women. What do you advise them about breast cancer screening? Select all that apply.

options.A: Women at increased risk for breast cancer include positive family history, genetic tendency, or past breast cancer
options.B: Obtain a mammogram yearly starting at age 40
options.C: Women at increased risk may require additional tests such as ultrasound or MRI
options.D: Mammograms expose the client to considerable doses of radiation and should only be done when abnormalities in the self-breast exam are noted

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, & C. The American Cancer
explanation: Society recommends a yearly mammogram for all women beginning at age 40. The organization defines women at increased risk of breast cancer and recommends earlier mammograms and additional testing if warranted.

question: All 50 states perform some type of newborn screening on each newborn client. The main purpose of this blood test procedure is:

options.A: Assessment of the visual acuity of the newborn client
options.B: Screening the newborn client for hearing loss
options.C: Evaluation of each newborn client for autism
options.D: Detection of disorders not readily apparent at birth

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Newborn screening programs iden-
explanation: tify newborn clients with rare disorders, which may cause developmental delay, mental retardation, serious medical problems, or death. Some disorders currently have no treatment. However, for those disorders for which treatment is available, serious morbidity and mortality can be avoided. The test requires a few drops of blood from a heel stick. This test does not assess vision, hearing, or autistic tendencies.

question: The incidence of melanoma rises rapidly in Caucasians after age 20. Clients at high risk require screening. The greatest risk for melanoma development is in clients with:

options.A: Fair skin who experience sun exposure
options.B: Pigmented lesions such a dysplastic or atypical nevi
options.C: Several large nondysplastic nevi
options.D: Many small nevi or moderate freckling

correctAnswerSourceText: A. The best defense against any skin
explanation: cancer, especially melanoma, is protection from the sun and ultraviolet light. Melanoma accounts for 75% of skin cancer deaths. The number of pigmented lesions also shows a relationship with the incidence of melanoma.

question: The most prevalent screening procedure for colorectal cancer includes:

options.C: DNA stool test for genetic changes

correctAnswerSourceText: B. A thin, tube-like instrument with a
explanation: light and lens for viewing is inserted into the rectum and sigmoid colon to ascertain the presence of polyps, abnormal areas, or cancer. The tool is equipped to remove polyps or tissue samples. A laparotomy and laparoscopic examination are not screening procedures. The DNA stool test for genetic changes in cells is being evaluated as a possible tool in colorectal cancer detection.

question: A monthly testicular self-exam is recommended for males to permit early detection and treatment of testicular cancer. Testicular cancer is more prevalent:

options.A: As male clients age with the highest incidence in the elderly
options.B: In male clients who have a second type of cancer
options.C: Among young, adult male clients between 20 and 35 years of age
options.D: In male clients with mental retardation

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Testicular cancer is rare, but in young
explanation: adult males the incidence is the most common type of cancer. Risk factors include positive family history, gonadal dysgenesis or Klinefelter’s syndrome, cancer in one testicle, and white race. While some testicular cancers are discovered by routine physical examination, the majority are detected by the patient. Therefore, routine self-examinations are recommended. Older clients are at less risk for testicular cancer. Clients with testicular cancer are at a higher risk for a second type of cancer, but another type of cancer does not predispose the client to testicular cancer. Male clients with mental deficits not attributable to chromosome abnormalities are not at an increased risk for testicular cancer.

question: A client reports to the nurse in a college student health clinic for minor injuries associated with a fall. Upon further questioning, the client states she is a freshman and that he also misses class usually on Monday mornings. The nurse should screen this client for:

options.C: Unsafe sex practices

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Young adults away from home for the
explanation: first time may engage in high-risk behaviors. Over 40% of college students report binge drinking and half of them report frequent binge drinking. Injuries such as falls and inability to attend class are signs of binge drinking.

question: The nurse overhears the spouse of an alcoholic client telling the client to “be quiet and don’t tell the physician anything about your drinking problem.” The nurse recognizes:

options.A: The spouse is exhibiting codependent behavior
options.B: The spouse is the person of authority in this marriage
options.C: The client has no choice but to follow the spouse’s instructions
options.D: The nurse must pretend not to have overheard this private conversation

correctAnswerSourceText: A. The spouse is exhibiting codependent
explanation: behavior by refusing to change her own attitudes and by focusing on controlling the alcoholic client. The nurse can benefit the couple by helping the spouse to disregard the alcoholic client’s promises, developing less dependence on the opinions of others, learning to set boundaries, expressing feelings, living in the present moment, and moving toward serenity, self-esteem, and independence.

question: The adventure-seeking teenager who gets bored easily and requires action, movement, and quick changes is at risk for drug and sexual experimentation. The nurse counsels the client and family to avert these high-risk behaviors by:

options.B: Working with a mental health specialist
options.C: Engaging in physical activities that allow the client to push the limits

correctAnswerSourceText: C. High-risk teenagers push the limits in
explanation: everything they do. The novelty-seeking teenager benefits from activities like rock climbing, mountain biking, kayaking, and team sports. These activities provide healthy stimulation while teaching delayed gratification, consequences for actions, and how to get along with others in society. While an after-school job and volunteer work may be positive behaviors,they don’t provide the sense of independence and accomplishment needed by adventureseeking teenagers. Counseling may help a high-risk teenager to understand his urges and consequences but again,does not provide the excitement the highrisk teenager seeks.

question: When screening a client for high-risk behaviors the nurse should (select all that apply):

options.A: Use medical jargon to educate the client about proper terminology
options.C: Initially use questions that are direct and target specific behaviors
options.D: Open with a statement such as “I discuss behaviors with all clients as part of their medical care.”

correctAnswerSourceText: B & D. Introductory statements that are
explanation: nonthreatening prevent the client from feeling targeted.Open-ended questions produce detailed client responses and should begin with less threatening questions and then move to more direct questions.A nonjudgmental, comfortable demeanor establishes trust.

question: A female, teenage client is seen in clinic today for a routine physical examination. During the screening for high-risk behaviors, the client tells the nurse that while she does not drink alcoholic beverages, her boyfriend does prior to driving an automobile. The nurse counsels the client to:

options.B: Refuse to ride with anyone who has been drinking alcoholic beverages
options.C: Drive herself home even though the client does not have a valid driver’s license yet

correctAnswerSourceText: B. A client should never ride with a
explanation: driver who has been drinking. Alcohol impairs judgment and places all riders at risk for injury or death. Alternate methods to arriving home include calling a sober, responsible person. Not dating the boyfriend is an option if the boyfriend refuses to change his behavior. Driving without a valid license is illegal. Threatening the boyfriend is not therapeutic.

question: A client is perimenopausal.She asks the nurse about the need for birth control. The nurse knows:

options.A: Birth control should continue until menstrual periods have been absent for at least 1 year
options.B: The client requires evaluation of folliclestimulating and leutinizing hormone levels
options.C: Estrogen replacement therapy is warranted
options.D: Sexual activity should be avoided during this time

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Irregular menstrual periods associated
explanation: with perimenopause leave the client vulnerable to an unplanned pregnancy if the client is sexually active. Hormone levels are useful to determine if the client is perimenopausal. Hormone measurement CHAPTER 17 ✚Sample Test Questions 399 and hormone replacement therapy are not forms of birth control. Being perimenopausal does not preclude sexual activity.

question: The nurse counsels a postmenopausal client:

options.A: It would be advisable to continue to use birth control
options.B: The risk of sexually transmitted infections decreases as age increases
options.C: Abstinence from sexual intercourse is advised
options.D: After menopause, sexually transmitted infections can still occur

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs)
explanation: do not discriminate based on age or sexual orientation. Postmenopausal clients who are sexually active should use precautions, such as condoms, to prevent STIs. Statistics show the rate of HIV infection in people over 50 years old is increasing. Birth control is no longer needed in the postmenopausal client. Abstinence will prevent STIs but abstinence is not an option in a client who remains sexually active.

question: A male client asks the nurse about the use of withdrawal (coitus interruptus) as a method for birth control. The nurse advises the client:

options.A: To use this method as a reliable form of birth control
options.B: That the effectiveness of this method is poor
options.C: That the sexual experience will not be altered
options.D: That coitus interruptus prevents sexually transmitted infections

correctAnswerSourceText: B. In coitus interruptus, the couple
explanation: engages in penile-vaginal intercourse. The penis is withdrawn from the vagina and female genital area when ejaculation is about to occur. It involves no cost, devices, or chemicals. However, the chance of pregnancy is higher (80% to 90%) than with any other method. Some men cannot gage ejaculation and may not withdraw in sufficient time. Interruption of the sexual response may decrease pleasure.There is no protection from sexually transmitted infections.

question: Teenagers who make virginity pledges begin engaging in vaginal intercourse later than those who have not made such pledges. The nurse is aware that (select all that apply):

options.A: Teenagers who take virginity pledges are more likely to engage in oral or anal sex than nonpledging, virgin teenagers
options.B: Both groups have an equal number of sexual partners
options.C: Pledgers have similar rates of sexually transmitted infections (STI) as nonpledging teenagers
options.D: Teenagers who make virginity pledges are more likely to use condoms when they become sexually active

correctAnswerSourceText: B & C. Teenagers who take virginity
explanation: pledges initiate sexual activity 18 months later than nonpledgers and have fewer sexual partners. However, they are less likely to use condoms once they become sexually active, undergo STI testing, and know their STI status. They view oral and anal sex as not “real sex,” placing them at risk of contracting STIs. They exhibit rates of STIs similar to nonpledgers.

question: Human sexuality education for clients with special needs:

options.A: Is not appropriate, especially for clients with intellectual disabilities
options.B: Is time consuming and often frustrating for client and educator
options.C: Should focus on genital sex rather than the expanded attributes of body image and social relationships
options.D: Improves social skills, reduces the risk of sexual abuse and sexually transmitted disease, and prepares clients for adulthood

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Like all children, clients with devel-
explanation: opmental disabilities grow into adolescence with physically maturing bodies and emerging social and sexual feelings and needs. It is important that parents, educators, and health care personnel overcome cultural barriers to healthy sexuality in clients with special needs and prepare them for adulthood by providing information in a positive and constructive way that is both clear and educationally appropriate.

question: A client is exposed to an organism that causes disease. The physician prescribes an immunoglobulin to prevent illness. This is an example of:

options.C: Acquired immunity

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Passive immunity is provided by the
explanation: administration of antibodies (immunoglobulins) produced by other people or animals. With active and acquired immunity the client is exposed to the antigen and produces his own antibodies.With herd immunity the individual is not immunized but the people around him are. This greatly decreases the chances the individual will develop the disease.

question: The nurse explains to a client that a vaccine is:

options.A: A medication that prevents an immune response
options.B: A serum protein noted with immunologic deficiencies
options.C: A suspension of bacteria or viruses that are nonpathogenic
options.D: A substance which destroys invading organisms

correctAnswerSourceText: C. A vaccine is nonpathogenic. It
explanation: induces, not prevents, an immune response. The total serum protein measures albumin and globulins. Decreased levels are present with malnutrition, liver disease, and immunologic deficiencies. A substance that destroys invading organisms is an immunoglobulin.

question: The most common side effects of vaccine administration are: 401

options.A: Unconsolable crying for several hours and refusal to eat
options.C: Soreness at the injection site and fever

correctAnswerSourceText: C. The most common side effects of
explanation: immunizations are minor and include injection site redness and discomfort, elevated temperature, and mild rash. Unconsolable crying, anaphylaxis, and shock are adverse events, not side effects. They are uncommon events with vaccine administration.

question: A student nurse asks the clinical instructor where there is an accurate place to obtain information regarding immunizations. The instructor recommends:

options.A: Looking up each vaccine in a current drug handbook
options.B: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention website
options.C: Seeking information from the pharmaceutical manufacturer of each vaccine

correctAnswerSourceText: B. The Centers for Disease Control and
explanation: Prevention (CDC) website contains a wealth of information on each vaccine and updates information throughout the year as it becomes available. The site also publishes vaccine recommendations for children, adults, individuals who need to “catchup” vaccinations, travelers to foreign countries, state-by-state school requirements, and special considerations such as recommendations for immunocompromised clients and clients with allergies to ingredients in a particular vaccine. A drug handbook and manufacturer information contain data about a specific vaccine. They do not contain the remainder of information available from the CDC website.A physician may be an incomplete source of information. 402 MARLENE HURST ✚Hurst Reviews: NCLEX-RN® Review

question: The component of a person’s lifestyle that primarily affects health status is:

options.B: Having earned at least a high school diploma
options.C: Owning a pet

correctAnswerSourceText: A. The diet is influential in promoting
explanation: health by providing necessary nutrients for growth and repair. Unhealthy patterns of eating lead to obesity, hypertension, diabetes, and cancer. Studies have shown a correlation between education and caring for a pet and health of the individual. Computer skills may permit an individual to obtain information about health and disease.

question: A client tells the nurse,“There’s no point in quitting cigarette smoking at my age. I have smoked for 40 years.” The nurse:

options.A: Understands that this is accurate since the client already has pulmonary disease
options.B: Tells the client that the progression of pulmonary disease may be halted with smoking cessation
options.C: Encourages the client to switch to smokeless tobacco use
options.D: Discusses the combination of pulmonary diseases that are the result of cigarette smoking

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Cessation of smoking interrupts the
explanation: progression of processes such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. It cannot stop cancer that is present but contributes to cancer therapy by eliminating vasoconstriction, thus permitting chemotherapeutic agent penetration. Cessation of smoking prevents further injury. Tobacco usage in any form is detrimental to health. Discussing pulmonary complications of smoking is informative to the client.

question: During a yearly physical examination, a client tells the nurse that the client “is stressed to the max” by work and family obligations. First, the nurse:

options.A: Encourages the client to speak with the physician
options.B: Suggests the client obtain a prescription for sleep aid medication
options.C: Discusses positive options for stress reduction
options.D: Counsels the client to consider a career change

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Positive options for stress reduction
explanation: include healthy diet, normal weight, regular exercise, and sufficient rest and sleep. It is important to educate the client that overeating,sedentary lifestyle,and chemical agents such as alcohol, nicotine, and caffeine are detrimental to health and have negative effects on stress reduction. While discussing the client’s stress with the physician is beneficial, it is not the nurse’s first action. Sleep aids and career changes do not address the complete problem.

question: Altered responses to lifestyle choices include (select all that apply):

options.C: Black lung (pneumoconiosis) in a coal miner

correctAnswerSourceText: A, C, & D. The association between
explanation: obesity and hypertension, inhaling coal dust and black lung, and sun exposure and skin cancer are well known. These disease processes are a direct result of the client’s lifestyle choices.

question: A young, adult client has a family history of chronic lung disease. He wants to avoid these processes and asks the nurse for information. The nurse replies:

options.A: There is nothing that can alter your genetic makeup
options.B: Chronic lung disease affects the elderly
options.C: You will not have lung disease if you do not smoke cigarettes
options.D: Occupational exposure to inhaled toxic agents leads to lung disease

correctAnswerSourceText: D. The environment has a major influ-
explanation: ence on health. Inhaled toxic agents such as asbestos and coal dust lead to debilitating pulmonary disease and death. Genetics cannot be altered but this response does not provide the information that the client seeks. Many forms of lung disease begin with chronic exposure to agents as a teenager or young adult and manifest well before becoming elderly. Cigarette smoking is a leading cause of lung disease, but individuals who have never smoked also develop pulmonary disease.

question: A nurse works in a clinic where the nurse is responsible for client education.Which principle is a factor in client education?

options.A: Every client is a learner throughout life
options.B: Learning is difficult for the very young and very old client
options.C: Middle-aged clients are busy with work and family and cannot focus on learning
options.D: Clients learn best when they are faced with a serious illness

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Each client learns throughout his or
explanation: her lifetime within social and cultural contexts and interactions with others. All clients including the young, middle-aged, and elderly can and do CHAPTER 17 ✚Sample Test Questions 403 learn. A serious illness poses severe stress on a client and actually may interfere with learning.

question: The nurse understands that one of the most vital aspects of teaching includes:

options.A: Relaying accurate information to the client
options.B: Asking the client what the client feels and needs to know
options.C: Identifying the way a client learns best
options.D: Having the client take a short pre- and post-test on the material

correctAnswerSourceText: C. The nurse can target client education
explanation: when the way a client learns is utilized. Visual learners need pictures or diagrams while others learn best by listening to information. Accurate information is imperative, but if not provided in a way the client learns best vital information may never be learned. The nurse should teach the information that the client needs to know. Taking tests is time consuming and not warranted. Assessment of the client’s knowledge base before teaching begins can be accomplished by asking direct and indirect questions. At the conclusion of the education session, the nurse can ask the client to summarize what he has learned.

question: The nurse is most likely to be an effective educator of clients when:

options.A: The nurse has complete content expertise
options.B: The nurse displays listening skills and receives feedback
options.C: The relationship between nurse and client is formal and impersonal
options.D: The nurse understands that good educators are born, not made

correctAnswerSourceText: B. In establishing a relationship with
explanation: the client learner, the nurse develops interaction and understands communication is from nurse to client and client to nurse. Two way communication is invaluable. The nurse educator has considerable knowledge regarding a topic. However, if content expertise is lacking the effective educator will refer the client to someone with the necessary information. The nurse facilitates and has expertise but does not need to know everything. The relationship between the nurse and client can be professional without being impersonal. Educators improve their skills when they learn and apply principles of learning and communication.

question: For a client to learn information, which must be present? Select all that apply.

options.A: The learning experience must have a clear purpose
options.B: The learner can regain his health
options.C: The learning experience is inclusive of all necessary information
options.D: The learner must be actively engaged

correctAnswerSourceText: A & D. The client must see the activity
explanation: as purposeful with focused objectives and outcomes. Relevant information is better received and assimilated.Active, hands-on, concrete experiences that employ a variety of media allow the client to learn by doing and by analogy. These activities are engaging to the client and are highly effective in promoting education. Education benefits the client, but may not restore health. Educational sessions that are too long may tire and overwhelm the client. Depending on the amount of material needing to be covered and the client’s condition, it may be more beneficial to break the content into shorter sessions with a direct focus.

question: The nurse educator knows that a client will understand and recall material better if the learning environment includes problem-based as well as knowledge-based activities. Which is an example of a problem-based activity?

options.A: The client recalls the symptoms of the client’s disease
options.B: The client comprehends the client’s medication regimen
options.C: The client can analyze the client’s glucometer value and determine what action is needed
options.D: The client performs a self-care activity accurately

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Problem-based learning involves
explanation: higher-order thinking skills such as analysis, synthesis, and evaluation. Knowledge-based learning involves recall, comprehension, and application.

question: A client has asthma. The nurse is aware that:

options.A: A written asthma plan and peak expiratory flow measurements foster self-care
options.B: Asthma education (information) improves health outcomes in adults
options.C: Regular, ongoing reviews of client education are not necessary or beneficial
options.D: Clients with asthma have the same incidence of hospital admissions, unscheduled physician visits, and missed days of work as clients without asthma

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Education regarding the disease, self-
explanation: management, and regular review by health care providers improves health outcomes for adults with asthma. Self-monitoring by peak expiratory flow or symptoms together with a written action plan produces positive results. Information alone does not improve outcomes. Clients with asthma are more likely to require unplanned care.

question: As winter approaches, the nurse counsels an elderly client:

options.A: To remain indoors as much as possible
options.B: That he needs thermal protection when outdoors
options.C: To consider spending the winter in a milder climate
options.D: That he will likely become ill if he does not remain in an environment with a constant temperature

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Clients, especially the older adult,
explanation: require attention to environmental temperature variations. Winter temperatures can quickly lead to hypothermia in an elderly client due to reduced subcutaneous fat, skin thinning, and reduced sensation, especially in the extremities. Hyperthermia is an opposite concern in the summer.

question: Self-monitoring of blood glucose is an important part of diabetes management because:

options.A: An elevated blood glucose level prompts the client to exercise and thus lower the value
options.B: An abnormal blood glucose value indicates the client is ingesting too many carbohydrates
options.C: It enables the client to make self-management decisions
options.D: Monitoring alerts the client that his insulin is not effective, and he should open a new vial

correctAnswerSourceText: C. By being aware of the blood glucose
explanation: value, the client can adjust diet, exercise, and medications. This process also informs the client of episodes of hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, which is important in fostering tight control of blood glucose values and preventing complications of the disease process. Elevated levels may indicate a worsening condition but may also represent stress and infection.

question: Self-care behaviors are vital to health promotion because (select all that apply):

options.A: They are a complement to professional health care
options.B: Self-care makes the client completely responsible for his behaviors and outcomes
options.C: The client is empowered to actively participate in fostering his own health
options.D: Employers do not raise health care premiums for healthy employees

correctAnswerSourceText: A & C. Self-care decisions improve
explanation: health or assist with a health problem. Such decisions include diet, exercise, rest and stress reduction, substance reduction or elimination, and education. They also include the client’s learning from past experience. These activities are empowering. Coupled with regular professional care, the health, well-being, and quality of life of the client is promoted.

question: As clients age, the nurse should remember that self-care practices by the client:

options.A: Result in a failure of the client to utilize medical services
options.B: Have little or no effect on mortality, but do reduce the overall rate of illness
options.C: Are limited in the ability to influence health and well-being
options.D: Promote health of the client now and in the future

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Self-care is the enhancement of health
explanation: and independent functioning through self-initiated behaviors. The health of elderly clients is significantly determined by patterns of living in young adulthood through middle age. Health behaviors now influence present and future morbidity and mortality. Self-care is intertwined with professional health care in meeting the needs of the individual.

question: A 75-year-old client exhibits diminished but equal peripheral pulses and cool hands and feet. The nurse’s most appropriate action is to:

options.B: Place the client on a cardiorespiratory monitor and assess the client for possible atriaventricular block
options.C: Understand these are normal gerontological changes caused by diminished inotrophy and arterial rigidity
options.D: Initiate oxygen therapy and call the code team

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Gerontologic differences in cardiovas-
explanation: cular assessment include decreased contractility (decreased myocardium,ventricular wall thickening, slow ventricular relaxation) and increasing arterial rigidity (reduction in elastin and smooth muscle). Notification of the physician is not urgent. A cardiorespiratory monitor, oxygen therapy, and resuscitation are not indicated.

question: When performing a physical examination on a 2-year-old client, the nurse:

options.A: Performs a head-to-toe examination in the same manner as a physical examination performed on an adult client
options.B: Sedates the client to achieve cooperation
options.C: Performs the minimally invasive maneuvers such as the examination of the ears and eyes at the beginning of the exam
options.D: Listens to the heart, lungs, and bowel sounds first

correctAnswerSourceText: D. A pediatric client requires a complete
explanation: physical examination just like the adult client. However, initially when the client is generally quieter, listening to various sounds using the stethoscope is recommended. Sedation is not warranted. Invasive procedures which may scare the client and result in loss of cooperation and initiation of resistant behaviors or crying should be performed last.

question: A student nurse is having difficulty determining the liver span of a client. The experienced nurse educates the student:

options.A: Since the liver span varies considerably between individuals, its measurement is of little value
options.B: To percuss in the midclavicular line from the nipple line downward and the iliac crest upward
options.C: To palpate the position of the liver first, and then attempt to percuss its position
options.D: That having the client flex his knees will relax the abdominal musculature

correctAnswerSourceText: B. In normal clients the liver is located
explanation: in the midclavicular line on the right. The average liver span is 2.5 to 5 inches (6 to 12 cm). By percussing from the nipple line downward and the iliac crest upward, the examiner can accurately assess liver span. This value is useful in determining normalcy versus a disease state and is part of the physical examination. The correct order of abdominal examination is inspection, auscultation, percussion, and palpation. Knee flexion relaxes abdominal muscles but may hinder liver span measurement.

question: When assessing the cardiovascular system the nurse inspects and palpates blood vessels. A rigid (hard) blood vessel will vibrate. The correct term for a palpable vibration of a blood vessel is:

options.C: Thrill

correctAnswerSourceText: C. The pulse in a normal vessel feels like
explanation: a tap. In a narrow or bulging vessel, the pulse feels like a vibration and is called a thrill. A bruit and a murmur are sounds due to turbulent blood flow. A heave is a bounding pulse that moves the examiner’s finger, hand, or stethoscope upward and outward away from the body.

question: The Neuman’s Systems Model maintains that each person (or group of persons) constitutes a system of five variables: physiological, psychological, sociocultural, developmental, and spiritual. These variables exist along a developmental continuum. The spiritual continuum can range from lack of awareness or denial of spirituality to a highly developed spiritual consciousness. A nurse who allows Neuman’s Systems Model to guide practice should address the client’s level of spiritual awareness or development and address any identifiable spiritual needs occurring in reaction to the:

options.A: Attitude clients choose in response to suffering
options.B: Availability and efficacy of resources for coping with the stressor
options.C: Meaning of this experience for the client

correctAnswerSourceText: D. The Neuman’s Systems Model
explanation: addresses any identifiable spiritual needs occurring in reaction to the stress of surgery. Travelbee’s theory of nursing makes an effort to ascertain the meaning of this experience for the client. Frankl’s CHAPTER 17 ✚Sample Test Questions 407 D. Focuses on different walking maneuvers (heelto-toe, tandem, heel walking) to evaluate neuromuscular function. Answer: B. Many elderly clients have sensory deficits and distractions can be confusing and limit the ability to thoroughly assess the client. Hopping, deep knee bends, and walking maneuvers can be difficult due to limited range of motion, decreased reflexes, and diminished sense of balance. Pulmonary changes in the elderly include decreased force of expiration, weakened cough reflex, and shortness of breath. Deep breaths, breath holding, and forced expiration may compound respiratory difficulty.

question: The theoretical support for spiritual caregiving is recognized by professional organizations that influence nursing practice and education. Some professional organizations have issues mandating that nurses offer spiritual care to clients and teach spiritual care to nursing students. Which organization meets these criteria?

options.A: American Nurses Association’s (ANA) Code for Nurses
options.C: Joint Commission on the Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations (JCAHO)

correctAnswerSourceText: C. JCAHO specifies that all clients be
explanation: assessed for spiritual beliefs and practices and have access to spiritual support. The ANA’s Code for Nurses states that nurses will respect the dignity and uniqueness of each client regardless of personal attributes. There is no State Nurses Association’s Policy & Procedure. DHS does not issue mandates for spiritual care.

question: Nurses sometimes perceive barriers to providing spiritual care. These barriers include (select all that apply):

options.C: Confusion about what spiritual care is
options.D: Lack of knowledge and preparation for spiritual caregiving

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C & D. All of the answer choices
explanation: are correct. Nurses sometimes perceive barriers to providing spiritual care. These barriers include a perceived lack of time, ability, lack of knowledge and preparation for spiritual caregiving, orientation to nursing care that emphasizes the biologic, and confusion about what spiritual care is.

question: Ethical principles to guide spiritual care include: Select all that apply.

options.C: Justice

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Several ethical principles
explanation: to guide spiritual care include: • Beneficence (doing good for clients). • Nonmaleficence (doing no harm to clients). • Autonomy (respecting and supporting others’ rights to self-determination). • Justice (or fairness). • Fidelity (or faithfulness to previous agreements). • Veracity (or truth-telling).

question: Effective communication requires the nurse to recognize and respond to the client’s nonverbal as well as verbal messages. Nonverbal communication generally provides more accurate information about emotions than does verbal communication. Nonverbal communication includes (select all that apply):

options.C: Gestures

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Nonverbal communication
explanation: includes touch, body movements, facial expressions, gestures, posture and gait, and even the way people dress or otherwise decorate themselves.

question: Listening is an essential element of nursing activities that promote spiritual health. Key aspects of listening empathetically are:

options.A: Helping clients listen to the nurse
options.C: Recognizing the client’s inner response
options.D: Striving to hear all aspects of the client’s message

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Key aspects of listening empathically
explanation: are striving to hear all aspects of the client’s message, recognizing the nurse’s inner response, and helping clients to listen to themselves and make sense of the information they have received.

question: Techniques for empathic listening include:

options.A: Assuming an attitude of superiority or savior
options.B: Attending to nonverbal messages as well as verbal messages
options.C: Changing the topic of conversation to avoid emotional discomfort
options.D: Offering responses that preach or attempt to fix the client’s emotional pain

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Techniques for empathic listening
explanation: include maintaining an attitude of caring, placing full attention in the present moment and on the client to be present to their deepest moods, refraining from personal issues and stories, attending to clients’ feelings as well as thoughts, attending to nonverbal messages as well as verbal messages, being aware of inner responses to a client, allowing silence, accepting tears, and integrating verbal and nonverbal client messages when forming responses. Assuming an attitude of superiority, changing the topic of conversation, and offering responses that preach are not conducive to empathic listening.

question: In the Buddhist religion, the use of drugs and alcohol is:

options.C: Encouraged

correctAnswerSourceText: B. In the Buddhist religion, the use of
explanation: drugs and alcohol is strongly discouraged.

question: Which religion believes that physical disease results from good or bad karma (result of acts previously committed)?

options.C: Hinduism

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Buddhism believe that physical dis-
explanation: ease results from good or bad karma (result of acts previously committed). Hinduism believes that health results when body elements are balanced by consuming food and drink in the right way and time. Jews believe that sickness and suffering is explained by sin, physical and psychological causes, or even demons.

question: Which religion believes in final judgment that determines heaven or hell?

options.C: Hinduism

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Christianity believes in final judg-
explanation: ment that determines heaven or hell. Buddhism believes in reincarnation until Nirvana is attained. Hinduism believes in reincarnation. Judaism has no official stance on the existence of an afterlife.

question: Which religion worships Allah, performs ritual prayers five times per day with ablutions prior, and attends mosque or gathers with groups at noon on Fridays?

options.C: Judaism

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Believers in Islam worship Allah,
explanation: address their lay religious leaders as Imam, perform ritual prayers five times per day with ablutions prior, attend mosque or gather with a group at noon on Fridays, and do not eat pork. Hinduism, Judaism, and Mormons do not share these restrictions.

question: Which religious group may decline unnecessary health care procedures on Shabbat?

options.C: Jews

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Jews may decline unnecessary health
explanation: care procedures on Shabbat. Christian scientists refuse many medical interventions and prefer to see their own practitioners. Christians and Mormons do not share in this restriction.

question: Unique and salient religious beliefs and practices found across many different faith traditions include (select all that apply):

options.B: Use of religious objects and worship practices to commune with higher spiritual beings or a deity
options.C: Vegetarianism and abstention from pork or certain other meats
options.D: Weekly holy days or Sabbaths when persons attend religious services

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. All should be considered
explanation: in addition to solemn and festive annual holy days that commemorate an important historical event significant to the religious tradition. Prohibition of actions that are considered disrespectful of the sanctity of life are also beliefs found across many different faith traditions.

question: Which form of communication most likely informs a client about how sincere, interested, and receptive a nurse is toward the client?

options.C: Silence

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Body language reveals much about a
explanation: client’s emotional state. Conversely, body language informs clients about how sincere, interested, and receptive a nurse is toward them.

question: The nurse knows that family coping is influenced by the family’s (select all that apply):

options.C: Process

correctAnswerSourceText: A, C, & D. Family coping is influence by
explanation: the family’s structure, function, and process. The family’s resources such as time, energy, money, knowledge, skills, and past experiences also influence the ways members solve problems and cope with stress and crisis. Gender is not listed as an influence on family coping.

question: The nurse teaches the client who has recently lost a spouse that a number of factors influence grief and mourning. These factors include (select all that apply):

options.C: Nature and meaning of the loss

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. A number of factors influ-
explanation: ence grief and mourning. These include the nature and meaning of the loss, characteristics of the mourner, characteristics of the death, social factors, and psychological factors.

question: In every household, members have to decide the ways in which work and responsibilities will be divided and shared. Different roles include:

options.C: Provider

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Different household roles include
explanation: provider role, housekeeping and child care roles, socialization role, sexual and therapeutic roles, recreation role,and kinship role.Bidder,gender,and student do not describe ways in which responsibilities will be divided and shared. CHAPTER 17 ✚Sample Test Questions 411

question: Interactional sources of role strain are related to difficulties in the delineation and enactment of familial roles. Five sources of difficulties in the interaction process include (select all that apply):

options.C: Lack of role knowledge

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Five sources of difficulties
explanation: in the interaction process include inability to define the situation, lack of role knowledge, lack of role consensus, role conflict; and role overload.

question: The nurse is giving a facility inservice on the topic of domestic abuse. Health effects of domestic violence include (select all that apply):

options.C: Higher rates of sexually transmitted infections

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Health effects of domestic
explanation: violence include injuries from assaults; chronic health problems such as irritable bowel syndrome, backache, and headaches; increased unintended pregnancies, pregnancy terminations, and lowbirth-weight babies; higher rates of sexually transmitted infections, including HIV; and higher rates of depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder, self-harm, and suicide.

question: A nurse working in a Planned Parenthood clinic routinely asks clients about experiencing possible domestic violence. The advantage of this line of questioning is that it:

options.A: Alienates victims of abuse, thus increasing cooperation with members of the health care team
options.B: Assists the local police in maintaining local inmate populations
options.C: Assures that the truth is revealed
options.D: Maintains the safety of women experiencing domestic violence

correctAnswerSourceText: D. The advantages of routinely inquir-
explanation: ing about domestic violence include uncovering hidden cases of domestic violence, changing perceived acceptability of violence in relationships, increasing ease of women to access support services earlier, changing health professionals’ knowledge and attitudes toward domestic violence and reducing social stigma, and maintaining the safety of women experiencing domestic violence.

question: The nurse working in a long-term care facility knows that elder abuse most often consists of:

options.C: Physical abuse

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Elder abuse mostly consists of neglect
explanation: followed by physical abuse, financial or material exploitation, psychological or emotional abuse, and sexual abuse.

question: An example of internal family coping strategies includes:

options.A: Maintaining active links with community groups and organizations
options.C: Seeking and using spiritual supports

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Internal family coping strategies
explanation: include family group reliance including delegation; the use of humor and stress management tactics; increased sharing together—maintaining cohesiveness; controlling the meaning of the stressor/demand—cognitive refraining and passive appraisal; joint family problem-solving; role flexibility; normalizing; limiting leisure time and recreational activities; and accepting stressful events as a fact of life. Maintaining community relationships, seeking spiritual supports, and seeking professional help are examples of external family coping strategies.

question: An example of external family coping strategies include:

options.B: Limiting leisure time and recreational activities
options.C: Sharing concerns and experiences with relatives, friends, and neighbors
options.D: The use of humor and stress-management tactics

correctAnswerSourceText: C. External family coping strategies
explanation: include seeking information and professional help; maintaining active links with community groups and organizations; seeking and using social supports (informal and formal social support systems and self-help groups); seeking and using spiritual supports; and sharing concerns with experiences with relatives, friends, and neighbors. Joint family problem-solving, limiting leisure time and recreational activities, and the use of humor and stressmanagement tactics are examples of internal family coping strategies.

question: The nurse knows that traits of healthy families include (select all that apply):

options.C: Sharing leisure time

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Traits of healthy families
explanation: include communication and listening; fostering table time and conversation; affirming and supporting each member; teaching respect for others; developing a sense of trust, play, and humor; balancing the interaction among members; sharing leisure time; and exhibiting a sense of shared responsibility and service to others.

question: At different stages of life, families must master certain developmental tasks in order to maintain psychological health. Families with young adults who are launching into society have family developmental tasks to master including:

options.C: Maintaining a supportive home base
options.D: Thinking about the future, education, and work

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Families with young adults launching
explanation: into society have developmental tasks including maintaining a supportive home base, maintaining parental couple intimacy and relationship, and after a member moves out, reallocating roles, space, power, and communication. Families with adolescents have developmental tasks including thinking about the future, education, job, and work. Families with middle-aged parents have developmental tasks including maintaining kinship ties. Families with preschool children have developmental tasks including coping with energy depletion.

question: Family structure is the ordered set of relationships among family parts and between the family and other social systems. In determining the family structure, the nurse needs to identify the:

options.A: Age of the individual family members
options.B: Gender of the individual family members
options.C: Individuals who compose the family

correctAnswerSourceText: C. In determining the family structure,
explanation: the nurse needs to identify the individuals who compose the family and the relationships between them, the interactions between the family members, and the interactions with other social systems. Age, gender, and living arrangements of the members of the family are not factors that need to be identified.

question: The technology-driven, critical care environment is fast paced and directed toward monitoring and treating life-threatening changes in client conditions. To the families of critical care clients, four behaviors indicate caring. These include:

options.C: Touch

correctAnswerSourceText: C. The major types of behavior that
explanation: indicate caring to family members of critical care clients are touch; providing information; open, honest communication; and an intuitive ability to detect changes in both physiologic and psychosocial status.

question: Guided imagery is a form of alternative therapy. Guided imagery can frequently be used by the nurse to decrease stress, pain, and anxiety.Additional benefits of guided imagery include:

options.C: Increased length of stay

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Additional benefits of guided imagery
explanation: are decreased side effects, decreased length of stay, reduced hospital costs, enhanced sleep, and increased client satisfaction. Guided imagery is a low-cost intervention that is relatively simple to implement. The client’s involvement in the process offers a sense of empowerment and accomplishment and motivates self-care.

question: Acutely ill clients often experience high levels of physiologic and psychologic stress.Sources of physiologic stress in the acutely ill client are:

options.C: Pain

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Sources of physiologic stress in the
explanation: acutely ill client include medications,pain,hypoxia, decreased cerebral and peripheral perfusion, hypotension, fluid and electrolyte imbalances, infection, sensory alterations, fever, and neurologic deficits. Experiencing one or more of these stressors can completely consume all the client’s available energy and thoughts, thus affecting his or her ability to interact, comprehend, and respond to teaching.

question: When confronted with life-altering situations, both clients and families can experience emotional stress.Which are sources of emotional stress? Select all that apply.

options.C: Self-image change

correctAnswerSourceText: B, C, & D. Sources of emotional stress are
explanation: fear of illness, role change, self-image change, and uncertain prognosis. Other sources of emotional stress are isolation from other family members, disruption in daily routines, financial concerns, and unfamiliar critical care environments.

question: During the initial phases of a critical illness, feelings of disbelief and denial are common. Fear of death, loss, powerlessness, and helplessness may be experienced. Which educational techniques are most effective when teaching the client who experiences these emotions?

options.C: Orient teaching to the present

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Education during this
explanation: phase should be aimed at reduction of immediate stress, anxiety, and fear rather than future lifestyle alterations or rehabilitation needs.Clients and families may need to be refocused on the present and encouraged to not dwell on what might happen in the future.

question: During which stage of illness should the nurse orient teaching to meet the client’s family’s needs?

options.C: Identifying change

correctAnswerSourceText: D. As families begin to understand and
explanation: become more aware of the client’s current situation, feelings of hopelessness, anger, frustration, resentment, and guilt can occur. Eventually signs of hope and acceptance will emerge, signaling entrance into the reorganization and resolution phase. During this phase, the client’s family is more receptive to teaching and learning new information.

question: When admitting a new client to the unit, the nurse should (select all that apply):

options.A: Explain reasons for equipment, monitors, and associated alarms
options.B: Orientate to the unit environment (e.g., call light and bed controls). 415
options.C: Orient to unit routines and plan of care
options.D: Orient to the various care providers and services they deliver

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. All of the above should be
explanation: performed by the nurse including explaining all procedures and their expected sensations or discomforts both in the unit and off the unit. The client should also be oriented to medications given including name, purpose of administration, and side effects to report to the nurse or health care team.

question: Which action should be a part of the teaching by the nurse during a client’s discharge planning? Select all that apply.

options.C: Financial assistance

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, & D. Discharge planning should
explanation: include teaching of: medications, diet, activity, pathophysiology of disease, symptom management, special procedures and associated equipment, when to call the health care provider, and available community resources.

question: Several skin conditions that are of most importance in African-American clients include:

options.C: Keloids

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Several skin conditions that are of most
explanation: importance in African-American clients include: • Keloids—scars that form at the site of a wound and grow beyond the normal boundaries of the wound. They are sharply elevated and irregular and continue to enlarge. • Pigmentary disorders—areas of either postinflammatory hypopigmentation or hyperpigmentation, appear as dark or light spots. • Pseudofolliculitis—“razor bumps” and “ingrown hair” are caused by shaving too closely with an electric razor or straight razor. The sharp point of the hair, if shaved too close, enters the skin and induces an immune response as to a foreign body. The symptoms include papules, pustules, and sometimes keloids. • Melasma—the “mask of pregnancy” is a patchy tan to dark brown discoloration of the face more prevalent in dark pregnant women.

question: Which factor is most accurately linked to stress?

options.C: Improvement of mental disorders

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Decreased life satisfaction, the devel-
explanation: opment of mental disorders, the occurrence of stress-related illnesses—such as cardiovascular disease, gastrointestinal disorders, low back pain, and headaches—and decreased immunologic functioning, which has been implicated in a diagnosis of cancer, are linked to stress.

question: Environmental and social stressors that place children and adolescents at high risk for poor adjustment include? Select all that apply.

options.C: Personal safety concerns

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, & C. Environmental and social stres-
explanation: sors that place children and adolescents at high risk for poor adjustment are personal safety concerns, community violence, prolonged poverty, increased availability of drugs, homelessness, and AIDS.

question: The primary mode of intervention for stress management consists of:

options.B: Conditioning to avoid physiologic arousal resulting from stress
options.C: Decreasing resistance to stress
options.D: Minimizing the frequency of stress-inducing situations

correctAnswerSourceText: D. The primary mode of intervention
explanation: for stress management consists of minimizing the frequency of stress-inducing situations, increasing resistance to stress, and counterconditioning to avoid physiologic arousal resulting from stress. Changing the environment to decrease the incidence of stressors should be the “first line of defense.”When that is not possible, individual and family coping resources need to come into play to reinterpret stress as a challenge, increase resilience against stress, or decrease the health-threatening effects of stressors.

question: The nurse teaches a client who complains of stress that the most proactive approach to minimizing the frequency of stress-inducing situations is to (select all that apply):

options.C: Control others

correctAnswerSourceText: B & D. Changing the environment, when
explanation: it is possible, is the most proactive approach to minimizing the frequency of stress-inducing situations. Other approaches include avoiding excessive change and managing time effectively. Stress is increased by exposure to excessive change and by attempting to control the behaviors and actions of others.

question: Psychologic conditioning to increase resistance to stress focuses on:

options.C: Enhancing self-esteem

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Resistance to stress is achieved
explanation: through either physical or psychological conditioning. Physical conditioning for stress resistance focuses on exercise. Psychological conditioning to increase resistance resources focuses on enhancing self-esteem, enhancing self-efficacy, increasing assertiveness, setting realistic goals, and building coping resources.

question: General coping strategies identified to enhance stress resistance include (select all that apply):

options.C: Problem solving

correctAnswerSourceText: C & D. General coping resources identi-
explanation: fied to enhance stress resistance are self-disclosure, self-directedness, confidence, acceptance, social support, financial freedom, physical health, physical fitness, stress monitoring, tension control, structuring, and problem solving. CHAPTER 17 ✚Sample Test Questions 417

question: Social networks that provide support to a client can be categorized by (select all that apply):

options.C: Intensity

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Social networks can be
explanation: defined with size (actual number of individuals), composition (types of persons in the network,such as spouse or friends), geographic dispersion (distances separating network members), intensity (frequency and extent of contact with network members), density (extent to which members know and interact with each other),and homogeneity (similarity of network members on various characteristics).

question: Which are sources of client support? Select all that apply.

options.C: Peers

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Social support is defined
explanation: as a network of interpersonal relationships that provide companionship, assistance, and emotional nourishment. Several social support systems relevant to health have been identified: natural support systems (families), peer support systems, organized religious support systems, organized professional support systems, and organized self-help support groups not directed by health professionals.

question: Nurses work with dying clients and their families everyday. The needs of the families of dying clients are:

options.A: To allow the nurse to provide all of the care to the dying person
options.B: To chastise the physician and health care staff
options.C: To shun the dying person

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Needs of families of dying clients are
explanation: to be with the dying person and to provide help to the dying person; to be informed of the dying person’s changing condition and to understand what is being done to the client and why; to be assured of the client’s comfort and to be comforted; to ventilate emotions and to be assured that their decisions regarding care are sound; to find meaning in the dying of their loved one; and to be fed, hydrated, and rested.

question: Many facilities allow the client’s family to be present during resuscitative efforts of the client. What is the advantage to having family present during resuscitation of a client?

options.A: The client’s obstruction of the grieving process
options.C: The family’s feelings of helplessness
options.D: The family’s recognition that the client is dying

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Advantages to having family present
explanation: to watch nurses and physicians carry out resuscitative efforts of the client include recognizing that the client is dying, feeling helpful and supportive to the client and the staff, knowing that everything possible is being done to resuscitate the client, being able to touch the client while he or she is warm, saying whatever they need to say while there is still a chance that the client can hear, recognizing the futility of further resuscitation efforts, facilitating the grieving process, and accepting the reality of death.

question: The nurse should communicate the news about the death of a client to the family:

options.C: By telephone

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Communicating news about the death
explanation: of a client to the family should be done in person whenever possible. The ideal setting is in a private room that has seating available for everyone.

question: The nurse should demonstrate compassion and empathy when communicating news about the death of a client to the family. Which is an example of appropriate communication skills by the nurse during this situation?

options.A: He was on the vent for a short time
options.B: I am very sorry for your loss”
options.C: It’s okay. He is at peace now
options.D: We coded him. He just didn’t make it

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Avoiding clichés and unfamiliar jar-
explanation: gon such as “code” and “vent” are important communication skills for the nurse. Stating a simple condolence and offering to answer any questions is appropriate.

question: The nurse discusses organ donation with a family whose loved one has suddenly passed. Common courtesy and sensitivity to the family’s grief are important. Which action facilitates the family’s option of organ donation?

options.A: Assuring the family that the decision is not theirs to make
options.B: Asking the family about organ donation immediately following the client’s death
options.C: Using a private area to discuss organ donation with the family
options.D: Communicating about the loved one’s death after organ donation forms are signed

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Using a private area to discuss organ
explanation: donation with the family facilitates the option of organ donation. The family should be assured that organ donation is their decision to make. The family should be allowed time to absorb the news regarding their loved one’s death before addressing donation or signing donation forms. Informing the family of the possible benefits of donation, providing information that will assuage the family’s fears about donation, and providing time for families to be with their loved ones and deciding about their options also facilitate offering of the option of organ donation.

question: Some health care providers believe there are disadvantages to having families observe cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). These disadvantages are (select all that apply):

options.A: CPR is traumatic and frightening to watch
options.B: Families may interfere with protocols and procedures
options.C: Staff may become too stressed and distracted when family is present
options.D: There is not enough space at the client’s bedside for the CPR team as well as the family

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. All of the above are cor-
explanation: rect. Some health care providers also believe that there is an increased risk of liability, and staff is not available to provide family information and support during the resuscitation.

question: Which are the four factors that are helpful in readying families for hospital discharge? Select all that apply. 419

options.C: Misuse of coping strategies

correctAnswerSourceText: A & D. Four factors that are helpful in
explanation: readying families for hospital discharge are availability of social support, use of coping strategies, accessibility to personal resources, and knowledge of what to expect after discharge.

question: The nurse knows that families require coping skills to manage illness recovery at home. Which is an appropriate coping skill shown by the family?

options.B: Inability to manage worry and anxiety
options.C: Inability to seek help if needed

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Coping skills shown by the family dur-
explanation: ing a client’s illness recovery at home are problemsolving ability, ability to seek help if needed, ability to manage worry and anxiety, and ability to acquire needed information. Nurses need to assess family coping strategies to devise interventions that will fit the individual family’s needs.

question: Four categories of personal resources can help family members feel ready to take a client home from the hospital. Which should the nurse address with the client and family during discharge teaching? Select all that apply.

options.C: Self-confidence

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. Health and energy, posi-
explanation: tive health beliefs, self-confidence, and time are categories that need to be addressed by the nurse during discharge teaching. 420 MARLENE HURST ✚Hurst Reviews: NCLEX-RN® Review

question: Which have influenced clients’ treatment needs and the system of care delivery in psychiatric and mental health treatment? Select all that apply.

options.C: Increased outpatient care

correctAnswerSourceText: C & D. Increased outpatient care and
explanation: shortened hospital stays along with more manageable medication protocols have influenced clients’ treatment needs and the system of care delivery in psychiatric and mental health treatment.

question: Which percentage of those with mental illness receive treatment in the health care system?
correctAnswerSourceText: A. Only 25% of those with mental ill-
explanation: ness receive treatment in the health care system despite the prevalence of mental illness, its many consequences, and the existence of effective treatment.

question: One theory commonly used in family mental health nursing is Bowen’s family systems theory. The central assumption in this theory is that chronic anxiety is the underlying basis for dysfunction. The theory consists of eight interlocking concepts that address anxiety and emotional processes. This includes:

options.C: The family process system

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Bowen’s family systems theory con-
explanation: cepts include differentiation of self, triangles, the family projection process, the nuclear family emotional system, multigenerational transmission process, sibling position, emotional cutoff, and societal regression.

question: Major depression most prominently affects:

options.C: More women than men

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Major depression affects approxi-
explanation: mately twice as many women as men. Women who are poor, the less educated, the unemployed, or those on welfare are at highest risk for experiencing major depression.

question: The nurse is caring for a client who experiences battered women’s syndrome. The nurse knows that the four forms of abuse are (select all that apply):

options.C: Physical

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. The four forms of abuse
explanation: are emotional, neglect, physical, and sexual.

question: Three sets of factors place families at risk for child abuse and neglect. Parental risk factors that place families at risk for child abuse and neglect include:

options.A: The behavior issues of the child
options.B: The parent’s belief in emotional punishment
options.C: The parent’s strong friendships in the community
options.D: The abuse or neglect the parent suffered as a child

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Research indicates that there are three
explanation: sets of factors that place families at risk for child abuse and neglect: parental characteristics, child characteristics, and family ecosystem characteristics. Parental factors include the parent’s abuse or neglect suffered as a child, the parent’s belief in physical punishment, the parent’s unrealistic expectations of the child, the parent’s level of stress, the parent’s loner behavior with few friends,the parent’s vision that the child is willful and purposely “bad,” and the parent’s substance abuse.

question: Which factor most accurately reflects characteristics of the child that place families at risk for child abuse and neglect?

options.B: The child has a difficult personality
options.C: The family is socially isolated
options.D: The parent believes in physical punishment

correctAnswerSourceText: B. Research indicates there are three
explanation: sets of factors that place families at risk for child abuse and neglect: parental characteristics, child characteristics, and family ecosystem characteristics. Characteristics of the child that place the family at risk for child abuse and neglect are that the child is different as a result of illness, prematurity, or disability; and that the child is difficult (i.e., fussy, hyperactive, demanding).

question: Which is a familial factor that most accurately places a family at risk for child abuse and neglect?

options.A: The child has a difficult personality
options.B: The family has no history of abuse
options.C: The family is socially isolated

correctAnswerSourceText: C. Research indicates that there are
explanation: three sets of factors that place families at risk for child abuse and neglect: parental characteristics, child characteristics, and family ecosystem characteristics. Familial factors include the family’s level of stress, social isolation of the family, a patriarchal (male-dominated) household, and history of abuse in the nuclear or extended family.

question: Primary prevention of domestic abuse involves:

options.A: Conducting community classes to teach parents about normal developmental challenges
options.B: Early intervention to prevent or stop the violence
options.C: Identification of families at risk for violence
options.D: Strengthening individuals and families to enable them to better cope with life stressors

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Primary prevention of abuse involves
explanation: strengthening individuals and families to enable them to better cope with multiple life stressors. For example, nurses can conduct community classes to teach parents about normal developmental challenges, such as toilet training; ways to discipline without physical punishment; and methods of conflict resolution.Secondary prevention involves identification of families at risk for violence and those who are beginning to use violence, followed by early intervention to prevent or stop the violence.

question: When the family is faced with impending loss of a member,unresolved conflicts and relational patterns may become intensified. In assisting the family, the family mental health nurse may intervene by (select all that apply):

options.A: Eliciting the family’s multigenerational history of loss to better understand the meaning of the impending loss to the family
options.B: Guiding the family in constructively addressing unresolved conflicts and issues between family members and the dying individual
options.C: Helping the family to convey its feelings to the dying person and to say goodbye
options.D: Supporting family members through the bereavement process, while remaining alert to symptoms that suggest complicated bereavement and the need for additional intervention

correctAnswerSourceText: A, B, C, & D. All of these are interven-
explanation: tions that can be made by the mental health nurse when assisting the family who experiences impending loss of a member.

question: Sensitive and skilled end-of-life care for clients and family members is critical for gerontological family nurses. Which is a common concern for clients and families experiencing the end of life?

options.C: Maintaining public identity

correctAnswerSourceText: D. Six common concerns for clients and
explanation: families experiencing the end of life are management of symptoms, communication about treatment, making preparations for death, completing and contributing, maintaining personal identity, and perpetuating a trusting relationship with the nurse and physician.

question: Which questionnaire should the nurse use to screen a male client for alcohol abuse?

options.C: FACT

correctAnswerSourceText: A. The CAGE questionnaire is used to
explanation: screen a client for alcohol abuse. There is no such thing as the COPE questionnaire. There is no such thing as the FACT questionnaire. TACE is a 4-item questionnaire based on CAGE but for use with pregnant women.

question: Which is a self-help group for families of alcoholics?

options.C: Alcoholics Anonymous

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Al-Anon is for families who are at
explanation: risk for alcohol problems, or who have a problem drinker or alcohol-dependent individual in the family. Al-Avert is not a self-help group. Alcoholics Anonymous is a self-help group for clients who are alcohol-dependent. Narc-Anon is for clients who are narcotic dependent.

question: Clients who are alcohol dependent usually require a two-phase treatment regimen.Which is an example of an effective two-phase treatment regimen?

options.C: Rehabilitation and depression

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Detoxification ameliorates the symp-
explanation: toms of withdrawal. Rehabilitation helps the client avoid future problems with alcohol.

question: In a client with anorexia nervosa, the nurse expects to see:

options.C: Intense fear of weight loss

correctAnswerSourceText: A. Diagnostic criteria for anorexia ner-
explanation: vosa are the refusal to maintain weight at or above a minimally normal weight for age and height, intense fear of weight gain even though the client is underweight, amenorrhea, and a severe body-image disturbance in which weight has undue influence on feelings of self-worth. Recurrent episodes of binge eating occurs with bulimia nervosa.

question: In a client with bulimia nervosa, the nurse expects to see (select all that apply):

options.B: Feelings of self-worth unduly influenced by weight
options.C: Recurrent episodes of binge eating
options.D: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behavior to prevent weight gain

correctAnswerSourceText: B, C, & D. Diagnostic criteria for bulimia
